title: Test feed development for dietary exposures to nano- and microparticulate contaminants in fish
author: Lammel

steps.title: Prepare nanoparticle stock suspension
steps.instruction: Disperse the nanoparticles in Milli‑Q water using ultrasonication to obtain a stable stock suspension; take aliquots for size, shape, hydrodynamic distribution and concentration verification (e.g., TEM, DLS, ICP‑MS or spectrophotometry); add exactly 2.475 ml of the stock (or a characterised dilution) to a clean glass beaker (100 ml capacity, 50 mm diameter, 70 mm height). Prepare a second identical beaker with 2.475 ml Milli‑Q water for the control diet. If a second test compound is required, incubate it with the NP suspension under continuous stirring until equilibrium is reached and any organic solvent has evaporated.

steps.title: Pre‑sorb nanoparticles onto dry feed flakes
steps.instruction: Add dry commercial fish feed flakes weighing 2.5 g (corresponding to the 2.475 ml aqueous volume) to the NP‑containing beaker; let the flakes soak for at least 5 min so that nanoparticles (and any co‑spiked compound) sorb to their surface.

steps.title: Macerate and homogenize soaked flakes
steps.instruction: Using a stainless‑steel spoon, macerate the soaked flakes until a thick paste forms; continue mixing for a minimum of 5 min to achieve a homogeneous distribution of the nanoparticles.

steps.title: Scale up paste to target food mass
steps.instruction: Add further portions of dry flakes in small batches together with equal volumes of ultrapure water (example: three additions of 2.5 g flakes plus 2.5 ml water each). After each addition, macerate and homogenize for at least 5 min as described above, until the total desired food mass is reached.

steps.title: Adjust consistency with gelatin
steps.instruction: Stick the food paste to the wall of the beaker to create a free area at the bottom. For 20 g of paste, add 1 g gelatin (leaf or powder) and 5 ml Milli‑Q water. Let the gelatin soak for ≥5 min, then dissolve it by placing the beaker in or over a 40 °C water bath while stirring. Gradually intermix the dissolved gelatin into the paste and stir for at least 5 min. Use food‑grade gelatin (e.g., Dr Oetker) or, preferably, research‑grade gelatin (CAS 9000‑70‑8, Ph.Eur., VWR).

steps.title: Load paste into syringes and attach microlance
steps.instruction: Transfer the final food paste into disposable 5 ml syringes; attach a 1.20 × 50 mm microlance/hypodermic needle to the syringe adaptor. Choose syringes free of latex, rubber, silicone oil, styrene, DEHP or other lubricants. The microlance defines the maximum worm diameter (1.20 mm); smaller diameters can be obtained with a finer needle, larger diameters by extruding without a needle.

steps.title: Prepare cable‑tie guide dish
steps.instruction: Cut two cable ties to 4 cm length and glue them on the inner surface of a 60 mm tissue‑culture dish using silicone aquarium sealant (toxic‑additive‑free). Space the ties ≈2 mm apart to form a guide track. Cut a piece of graph‑millimeter paper to the dish size, glue it to the bottom with the graticule facing up. Add ice‑cold DI or Milli‑Q water until it slightly covers the guide track. (A plain plastic petri dish may be used, but the hydrophilic treated surface reduces water volume.)

steps.title: Extrude and cut worm‑shaped food rations
steps.instruction: Place the syringe tip at the opening of the guide track (position A) and gently press the plunger to extrude a food worm along the track toward position B. When the worm reaches the desired length, cut it at position A with a stainless‑steel scalpel or razor blade. Example: a 10 mm worm of 1.20 mm diameter weighs ≈7.6 mg; for a 1 g fish receiving 2 % body weight (20 mg) the required length is ≈26 mm. Syringes can be stored at 4 °C for use within the same week or at –20 °C for later use.

steps.title: Clean and feed food rations
steps.instruction: Using a disposable Pasteur pipette, remove any debris or released nanoparticles from the cut end of the worm; replace the water in the dish with fresh ice‑cold water. Gently collect the worm with the pipette and transfer it to the experimental aquarium. The rations may also be dried at room temperature or 40 °C to produce small pellets.

steps.title: Culture and depurate live worms
steps.instruction: Maintain Tubifex tubifex (or alternative prey such as red mosquito larvae) in a sediment‑free culture vessel with artificial freshwater for ~2 weeks to allow depuration. Collect the worms with a disposable Pasteur pipette and transfer them into a 13–15 ml round‑base reaction tube whose empty weight has been recorded.

steps.title: Homogenize worms and add red color
steps.instruction: Using a rotor‑stator tissue homogenizer (e.g., Labassco), homogenize the worms for ~30 s to obtain ~5 ml of homogenate. Spike the homogenate with red food colour at ≤5 % v/v to restore natural colour. Place the tube in a beaker of tepid tap water (30–40 °C) until all air bubbles rise and the foam largely disappears.

steps.title: Prepare gelatin solution and measure density
steps.instruction: Make a 0.3 g ml⁻¹ gelatin solution by soaking the appropriate amount of gelatin powder (CAS 9000‑70‑8, Ph.Eur., VWR) in ultrapure water; hold the reaction tube (e.g., 50 ml Falcon) in a 40–50 °C water bath while stirring with a stainless‑steel spoon until fully dissolved. For small volumes a 0.2 g ml⁻¹ solution may be used. Keep the solution in the warm bath until bubbles disappear, then take an aliquot, weigh it and record the density.

steps.title: Spike homogenate with nanoparticle stock
steps.instruction: Calculate the volume of NP stock needed to reach the desired µg NP g⁻¹ wet‑weight diet, taking into account the densities of the worm homogenate and gelatin solution and the planned 1:1 (v/v) mixing ratio. Transfer the bubble‑free portion of the homogenate to a new tube, add the calculated NP stock volume, and gently pipette up‑and‑down or stir (no vortex) until the nanoparticles are homogeneously dispersed. Use the smallest feasible NP‑stock volume that still allows accurate pipetting; adjust stock concentration accordingly.

steps.title: Combine homogenate with gelatin to form solid paste
steps.instruction: Mix the NP‑spiked homogenate with the gelatin solution in a 1:1 (v/v) ratio. Ensure the gelatin solution is bubble‑free (use bottom aliquot) and that the homogenate is at ~40 °C to avoid lump formation. The resulting mixture should have a dough‑like consistency suitable for extrusion.

steps.title: Load paste into syringes and gelatinise
steps.instruction: Draw the mixed paste into disposable 1 ml syringes equipped with a 1.20 × 50 mm microlance. Immediately place the syringes (caps removed) into an ice‑filled box to start gelatinisation. After 30–60 min transfer the syringes to a refrigerator, seal the needle tip with parafilm, and store at 4 °C overnight or until needed. Use syringes free of latex, rubber, silicone oil, styrene, DEHP, etc.

steps.title: Extrude and cut worm rations from liquid feed
steps.instruction: Prepare the cable‑tie guide dish as described in step 7. Remove syringes from the fridge, keep the caps off, and place the needle tips in ice. Fill the dish with ice‑cold water and extrude food worms along the guide track. Cut the worms to the required length (e.g., ~26 mm for a 20 mg dose) using a scalpel or razor blade, following the same procedure as in step 8.

steps.title: Clean and feed worm rations
steps.instruction: Using a disposable Pasteur pipette, wipe any debris from the cut end of each worm, replace the water in the dish with fresh ice‑cold water, then collect the worm with the pipette and transfer it to the aquarium containing the experimental fish. The rations may be dried at room temperature or 40 °C if pellet formation is desired.
